artifacts.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)
artifacts.purpose: Electric four-wheel rover to expand astronaut mobility and scientific sample collection
artifacts.status: Stationed permanently on lunar surface at Taurus-Littrow
artifacts.history: Built by Boeing and Delco, the Lunar Roving Vehicle allowed Apollo astronauts to travel up to 35 kilometers from their lunar module, dramatically expanding geological exploration.
artifacts.geological_context: Taurus-Littrow Valley floor regolith deposit adjacent to Camelot Crater
artifacts.measured_properties: Conductivity: High (Al alloy / Cu wiring), Depth: 6.5 cm, Magnetic Dipole: Moderate
artifacts.estimated_properties: Total Mass: ~210 kg, Structural Integrity: 88%, Soil Compaction: Low

artifacts.name: Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stage
artifacts.purpose: Rocket-powered descent platform and the base camp for humanity's first lunar landing
artifacts.history: On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin piloted the Eagle to the lunar surface. The descent stage remained on the Moon, serving as the launch pad for the astronauts' return to orbit.
sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
artifacts.geological_context: Mare Tranquillitatis basaltic regolith sheet, West Crater ejecta halo
artifacts.measured_properties: Conductivity: Very High (Titanium / Mylar shielding), Depth: 12.0 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Residual Propellant: Inert, Footpad Penetration: 7.6 cm into regolith

artifacts.name: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
artifacts.purpose: Nuclear-powered geophysical laboratory studying moonquakes, solar wind, and lunar atmosphere
artifacts.status: Deactivated in 1977 after collecting 8 years of seismic and thermal science
artifacts.history: Powered by plutonium-238 radioisotope generators, ALSEP stations transmitted continuous data on lunar seismology and magnetic fields back to scientists on Earth for nearly a decade.
artifacts.geological_context: High-porosity pyroclastic mantling deposit overlying sub-floor basalt
artifacts.measured_properties: Conductivity: High, Thermal Profile: Residual RTG dissipation footprint, Depth: 9.0 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Structural Housing: Intact cast Beryllium, Cabling: Partially regolith-cemented

artifacts.name: Sojourner Rover
artifacts.stratigraphic_layer: Windblown Basaltic Sand & Dust Mantle (0–7 cm)
artifacts.detection_signature: Aluminum Chassis & Silicon Solar Array Resonance
artifacts.geological_context: Ares Vallis catastrophic flood plain deposit resting near Yogi Rock
artifacts.measured_properties: Chassis: 7075-T6 Aluminum, APXS Instrument Head: Intact, Depth: 5.4 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Solar Array Dust Obscuration: 92%, Battery Charge: 0%, Mobility: Frozen
artifacts.purpose: Pioneering technology demonstration of the first wheeled rover on the Martian surface
artifacts.status: Mission completed; preserved at Ares Vallis
artifacts.history: The microwave-sized Sojourner rover operated for 83 sols (days) on Mars, traveling 100 meters, taking hundreds of images, and analyzing chemical composition of Martian rocks like 'Barnacle Bill'.

artifacts.name: Opportunity Rover (MER-B)
artifacts.stratigraphic_layer: Sulfate-Rich Evaporite Outcrop & Hematite Bed (0–12 cm)
artifacts.geological_context: Endurance/Perseverance Valley rim outcrop with exposed sulfate laminations
artifacts.measured_properties: Pancam Mast: Deployed, Rock Abrasion Tool: Bit worn, Depth: 9.8 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Dust Accumulation: Heavy ferric coating, Solar Cell Output: Negligible
artifacts.purpose: Search for geological evidence of past liquid water on Mars
artifacts.status: Completed mission in 2018 at Perseverance Valley after 14.5 years
artifacts.history: Planned as a 90-day mission, 'Oppy' drove 45.16 kilometers across Meridiani Planum, discovering hematite spherules ('blueberries') and rock layers formed in ancient standing liquid water.
sources: NASA JPL Mars Exploration Rover Archives

artifacts.name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
artifacts.stratigraphic_layer: Active Eolian Sand Ripple Deposit (0–4 cm)
artifacts.detection_signature: Carbon-Fiber Composite & Ultra-Light Lithium Cell Echo
artifacts.geological_context: Jezero Crater Neretva Vallis delta transition zone atop undulating sand ripples
artifacts.measured_properties: Rotor Span: 1.2 m counter-rotating, Carbon Blade Tip: Micro-fractured, Depth: 3.2 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Solar Panel: Partially dust covered, Avionics: Inactive, Fuselage: Pristine
artifacts.purpose: Technology demonstration of powered, controlled aerodynamic flight on another planet
artifacts.status: Grounded after rotor blade damage; completed 72 historic flights
artifacts.history: Weighing only 1.8 kilograms, Ingenuity made history on April 19, 2021 by achieving the first powered flight in the ultra-thin Martian atmosphere, acting as an aerial scout for Perseverance.

artifacts.name: Jezero Delta Smectite Clay Mudstone
artifacts.detection_signature: Hydrated Mineral Dielectric & High Iron-Magnesium Response
artifacts.geological_context: Fine-grained sedimentary bottomset bed deposited in tranquil ancient Jezero lake waters
artifacts.measured_properties: Fe/Mg Smectite Clay: 44%, Carbonates: 26%, Sulfate veins: 18%, Depth: 22.4 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Deposition Age: ~3.7 Ga (Noachian-Hesperian transition), Biosignature Potential: Prime
artifacts.purpose: Analyze ancient habitable lake environment and search for organic compounds preserved in fine sediment
artifacts.status: Sedimentary rock core target in Jezero delta front
artifacts.history: Drilled at Wildcat Ridge by the Perseverance rover, these clay-rich mudstones formed billions of years ago in mud that settled at the bottom of Lake Jezero, representing the most favorable environment for preserving evidence of past microscopic life.
sources: Science Advances: Aqueous Alteration in Jezero Delta

artifacts.name: Séítah Formation Olivine Cumulate
artifacts.detection_signature: High Magnetic Susceptibility from Magmatic Magnetite
artifacts.geological_context: Crater floor igneous cumulate layer modified by ancient water interactions
artifacts.measured_properties: Olivine: 65%, Pyroxene: 22%, Interstitial Carbonate/Sulfate, Depth: 34.0 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Crystallization Age: ~4.0 Ga, Magma Chamber Cooling Rate: Slow plutonic/thick lava flow
artifacts.purpose: Determine the age of Jezero Crater floor and decipher Mars's primordial volcanic evolution
artifacts.history: Perseverance's investigation of South Séítah revealed that the crater floor is composed of thick igneous cumulate rock rich in olivine grains, which formed as magma cooled slowly in a subterranean magma chamber or thick pond of lava.
sources: Science: Compositionally and Densitometrically Layered Igneous Rocks in Jezero Crater

artifacts.name: Perseverance Jettisoned Thermal Protection Tile
artifacts.detection_signature: Composite Inconel Fastener & Charred PICA Core Anomaly
artifacts.geological_context: Impact scatter perimeter 1.5 km south of the Octavia E. Butler landing site
artifacts.measured_properties: PICA Ablative Matrix: Surface char depth 4.2 mm, Titanium bracket, Depth: 6.8 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Atmospheric Entry Velocity: ~5.3 km/s, Aerothermal Peak Temperature: ~1300°C
artifacts.purpose: Ablative heat shield segment protecting the entry capsule during extreme aerodynamic heating
artifacts.status: Impact scatter remnant on Jezero plains
artifacts.history: On February 18, 2021, Perseverance's heat shield dropped away at high altitude during entry, descent, and landing (EDL), impacting the surface at terminal velocity and scattering engineered thermal tiles across the desert.
sources: JPL Entry Descent and Landing Systems Archive

artifacts.name: Impact-Preserved Martian Shergottite
artifacts.geological_context: Ejecta crest of Belva impact crater excavating deep volcanic crust
artifacts.measured_properties: Pyroxene: 58%, Maskelynite (shocked plagioclase): 32%, Shock veins, Depth: 16.5 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Peak Impact Shock Pressure: ~35 GPa, Cosmic Ray Exposure: 3.2 Ma
artifacts.purpose: Examine high-pressure impact metamorphism and noble gas atmospheric entrapment
artifacts.status: Weathered basaltic rock clast with desert varnish
artifacts.history: Shergottites are igneous basaltic rocks formed on Mars that have experienced intense shock pressures from meteorite impacts, converting feldspar into glass (maskelynite) and trapping ancient atmospheric gases inside impact melt veins.
sources: NASA Planetary Science Division Mars Meteorite Compendium

artifacts.name: Mars Pathfinder Lander (Carl Sagan Memorial Station)
artifacts.detection_signature: Folded Silicon Solar Petals & Vectran Airbag Core
artifacts.geological_context: Catastrophic outflow channel floodplain in Ares Vallis (19.33° N, 326.45° E)
artifacts.measured_properties: Petals: 3 deployable solar petals, Mass: 264 kg dry, Cameras: IMP stereo mast
artifacts.estimated_properties: Touchdown Velocity: 14 m/s cushioned by 24-lobe airbags, Total Sols: 83
artifacts.purpose: First low-cost Discovery mission to deploy a mobile microrover on Mars
artifacts.status: Stationary monument on Ares Vallis regolith
artifacts.history: Touched down July 4, 1997 using parachutes and innovative giant airbags. Served as communications relay and base station for Sojourner microrover before final transmission on Sept 27, 1997.

artifacts.name: Spirit Rover (MER-A)
artifacts.detection_signature: Rocker-Bogie Titanium Chassis & Seized Drive Wheel
artifacts.geological_context: Gusev Crater / Columbia Hills Home Plate plateau (14.57° S, 175.47° E)
artifacts.measured_properties: Total Traverse: 7.73 km, Right-front wheel: Jammed on Sol 779, Power: Faded solar arrays
artifacts.estimated_properties: Subsurface Silica Purity: 91% revealed by dragged wheel, Last signal: March 22, 2010
artifacts.purpose: Search for past water activity and hydrothermal deposits in Gusev Crater
artifacts.status: Stationary inactive rover embedded in sulfate sand at Troy
artifacts.history: Traveled 7.73 km across Gusev Crater and climbed Husband Hill. Uncovered nearly pure silica deposits indicating ancient hot springs before becoming immobilized in loose sand in late 2009.

artifacts.name: Viking 1 Lander
artifacts.geological_context: Chryse Planitia volcanic plains and flood deposits (22.27° N, 312.05° E)
artifacts.measured_properties: Power: 57 W from dual Pu-238 RTGs (NO solar cells), Mass: 612 kg landed
artifacts.estimated_properties: Operational Lifetime: 2,307 Sols (6.3 Earth years), Final transmission: Nov 11, 1982
artifacts.purpose: First successful long-duration Mars lander; conducted biological and atmospheric soil testing
artifacts.status: Stationary intact historical lander on Chryse plains
artifacts.history: On July 20, 1976, Viking 1 became the first American spacecraft to touch down successfully on Mars, capturing humanity’s first color surface photographs and operating for over 6 years.
sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

artifacts.name: Viking 2 Lander
artifacts.detection_signature: Dual SNAP-19 RTG Shrouds & Telescoping Arm
artifacts.geological_context: Dense rock field in Utopia Planitia (47.97° N, 134.29° E)
artifacts.measured_properties: Sampler reach: 3.0 m, Tilt angle: 8.2° on boulder field, Power: Dual SNAP-19 RTGs
artifacts.estimated_properties: Operational Lifetime: 1,316 Sols, Recorded seismometer data and winter water-frost
artifacts.purpose: Investigate northern volcanic plains, atmospheric meteorology, and search for biosignatures
artifacts.status: Stationary historical lander in Utopia Planitia rock field
artifacts.history: Landed September 3, 1976 amidst a vast field of vesicular basalt boulders. Its surface sampler arm dug trenches and its meteorology sensors documented seasonal thin water-ice frost coatings.

artifacts.name: Phoenix Mars Lander
artifacts.detection_signature: Dual Decagonal Circular Solar Wings & Carbide Rasp
artifacts.geological_context: Polygonal permafrost plains in Vastitas Borealis (68.22° N, 234.25° E)
artifacts.measured_properties: Solar span: 5.52 m, TEGA ovens: 8 miniature cells, Arm reach: 2.35 m
artifacts.estimated_properties: Verified Subsurface Ice: Sublimation of trench ice observed over 4 sols
artifacts.purpose: Confirm and analyze subterranean water ice in the Martian arctic plains
artifacts.status: Stationary arctic lander encased in winter carbon dioxide ice remnants
artifacts.history: Landed May 25, 2008 in the northern arctic plains. Its robotic arm scraped away loose red dust to uncover pure white water-ice permafrost only inches below the surface before polar darkness ended operations.
sources: University of Arizona Lunar & Planetary Laboratory

artifacts.name: InSight Mars Lander
artifacts.detection_signature: SEIS Wind Thermal Shield Dome & UltraFlex Arrays
artifacts.geological_context: Smooth volcanic plain in Elysium Planitia (4.50° N, 135.62° E)
artifacts.measured_properties: SEIS Sensitivity: Pico-meter vibrations, Recorded: 1,319 marsquakes, HP3 depth: 37 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Crustal Thickness: 24 to 72 km, Core Radius: ~1830 km (liquid iron-nickel)
artifacts.purpose: Investigate the deep interior seismology, crustal thickness, and core size of Mars
artifacts.status: Stationary inactive lander with SEIS dome on Elysium soil
artifacts.history: Operated from Nov 2018 to Dec 2022. Deployed the French SEIS seismometer onto the soil and mapped Mars’s crust, mantle, and molten liquid core before heavy atmospheric dust darkened its solar arrays.
